verdict.rationale: Unity's docs show a mature, long-standing public scripting API and extensive official manuals (unity-docs-11, unity-docs-6/7) that would plausibly be well-represented in LLM training data, and the product does provide an llms.txt at the root domain (unity-docs-15/16/31). However there is no direct evidence—benchmarks, community reports, or hands-on tests—showing LLM-generated Unity C# code actually works reliably on the first try, and probes show the docs subdomain lacks machine-readable formats (404s for llms.txt, docs-md, openapi at docs.unity3d.com) that would aid AI consumption. Missing for 10: empirical evidence of LLM code-gen success rate, community confirmation of first-try correctness, and consistent AI-friendly documentation formats across all doc surfaces.
